pairs.difference: A: orange locker against a purple wall, with blue sneakers, a red ball and warm wood. That is a warm hero on a cool backdrop with several distinct hue families, as on the real cards. B: a near-black joystick base on grey brushed steel. The only chroma is the small red ball, the yellow button and the flat green wall. The hero is almost colourless, the warm share is tiny (0.085) and the shadows turn to dead grey.
pairs.fix: Make the joystick base a coloured plastic, such as deep blue or purple, instead of black-on-steel. Put it on a warm wooden table and keep the red ball and yellow button as accents.

pairs.difference: A: the twin tanks are flat neutral grey with no hue. The orange nozzles are the only chroma, set on a single green sunburst. The whole card collapses to green plus grey (about 1.3 hue families), so the hero has no local colour. B: red velvet box, cream lining and a gold medal on a cyan sunburst. That is a warm hero on a cool backdrop with rich crimson shadows.
pairs.fix: Paint the jetpack tanks a coloured metal, such as red or orange enamel with a cream band. Keep the grey only on the small valves, and place it on a cool blue or teal sunburst.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket body is creamy off-white and the shadows on it go warm beige. The fins and flame are saturated orange. That is the same cream-whites drift that marked the generated computer and lighthouse in the lessons. B: the plane's white is a clean cool white with blue shading, set in a blue sky. The palette is monochrome, but the whites stay neutral.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocket body a clean neutral white with cool grey-blue shading, not cream. Make the fins and nose a deeper red-orange with darker red shadows.

pairs.difference: A: red gloves with deep crimson shadows against a blue plank wall and an orange wood table. The local colours are believable and the warm/cool contrast is strong. B: a silver pouch that is almost colourless (subject chroma 0.024), set on a cyan stripe wall and a white floor. Its shadows pick up cyan-blue from the backdrop, so the only warm note is the tiny red cap.
pairs.fix: Give the pouch a printed coloured label, such as orange or yellow with a fruit graphic, over a smaller silver area. Set it on a warm wooden table in front of the cyan wall.

pairs.difference: A: a red booth on a flat green patterned wall, with the green repeated in the glass panes. B: an orange-and-yellow seahorse on a deep blue underwater gradient, which is warm on cool. Both chroma levels and hue counts are within the real range, and neither shows the generated tells from the lessons.

A: a red bike on a pale blue car with a warm dusk sky. It has varied hue families, purple-blue shadows and believable local colour, which matches the real bike card. B: a white board with a red frame on a single cyan radial. The board's shading and the pole pick up the cyan, so its shadows are tinted by the backdrop (shadow chroma 2.46). There are only two hue families besides the orange rim.
pairs.fix: Put the hoop in front of a warm sunset sky or a brick wall instead of a flat cyan radial. Shade the white backboard with neutral grey, not cyan.

pairs.difference: A: the gloves are neutral white and grey with one thin orange band, sitting on a single violet field (about 1.2 hue families). The hero has almost no chroma and its shadows go violet from the backdrop. B: a saturated blue machine with multicolour cans and bottles inside, on magenta. The hero has its own local colours.
pairs.fix: Give the space gloves coloured panels, such as orange or red knuckle pads and blue cuffs, and keep the white limited to the main fabric. Put them on a warm yellow or orange backdrop instead of violet.

pairs.difference: A: the real lighthouse card. B: a grey metal porthole on a pink-lilac wall, whose shadows go mauve. The star window is a navy disc. The palette is pink plus a greyed violet, with no warm/cool contrast against a hero. The pink is pastel and low in chroma (0.07), and the warm share comes from the pink cast rather than from any local colour.
pairs.fix: Paint the porthole rim a warm brass or copper, and make the hull wall a cool teal or steel-blue panel with a few orange warning stripes. Keep the window deep blue with stars.

pairs.difference: A: blue sneakers with green and orange accents on an orange-and-cream setting. That is a cool hero on a warm backdrop, with many hue families. B: a white helmet with a gold visor on a hot pink field. The visor and the pink are both warm (warm share 0.907, above the real range), and the white shell goes pinkish-beige in shadow, so it repeats the backdrop instead of opposing it.
pairs.fix: Put the helmet on a deep blue or teal backdrop. Shade the white shell with cool grey-blue and keep the gold visor as the single warm accent.

pairs.difference: A: red brick posts, a copper gate and pink paving against green trees and a blue sky. Warm and cool are balanced, and the hero has plenty of local colour. B: the observatory dome and wall are nearly colourless off-white and grey (subject chroma 0.032). The only chroma is the green lawn, the blue sky and a small red door, and the dome's shadows go greenish-grey.
pairs.fix: Build the observatory walls from warm sandstone or red brick with a copper or teal dome, and keep the white only for trim.

pairs.difference: A: a yellow submarine with copper rims and cyan windows on a dark green radial. That is warm on cool, with rich ochre shadows. B: a purple saucer with a green dome on a yellow radial. The yellow glow washes into the dome and the beam, pushing the whole card warm (warm share 0.82, above the real range).
pairs.fix: Use a cool deep-blue or teal radial backdrop behind the purple saucer, and keep the light beam pale and neutral rather than yellow.

pairs.difference: A: the capsule's cone is neutral white with blue-grey shading, and its base is dark brown, set in a blue cloudy sky. The hero has almost no chroma (0.032) and only the small yellow window adds colour, so the white takes the blue of the sky. B: red, orange, teal and purple balloons in a blue sky, each with its own local colour and darker hue-related shadows.
pairs.fix: Paint the capsule's cone with orange or red heat-shield panels and a copper-brown base, and keep the white only on small trim. Use a warmer sky so the hero is warm against a cool backdrop.

pattern: Generated sci-fi props are drawn as neutral white, grey or silver with almost no local colour, such as the tanks, gloves, pouch, dome, capsule and porthole. Their shadows take the backdrop's hue (cyan, violet or pink) instead of a darker version of their own colour. The hero then repeats the background temperature instead of opposing it, so cards end up with one hue family plus grey. Where generated whites do carry colour, they drift to cream.
